passages.text: If you see your brother’s ox or sheep straying, you must not ignore it; be sure to return it to your brother.
passages.sermon:
God gave Israel laws for living together.
God told the people to care for each other’s property.
If you see your brother’s ox wandering away, do not ignore it.
If you see your brother’s sheep wandering away, do not ignore it.
You must return the animal to your brother.
passages.original: לֹֽא־ תִרְאֶה֩ אֶת־ שׁ֨וֹר אָחִ֜יךָ א֤וֹ אֶת־ שֵׂיוֹ֙ נִדָּחִ֔ים וְהִתְעַלַּמְתָּ֖ מֵהֶ֑ם הָשֵׁ֥ב תְּשִׁיבֵ֖ם לְאָחִֽיךָ׃

passages.text: If your brother does not live near you, or if you do not know who he is, you are to take the animal home to remain with you until your brother comes seeking it; then you can return it to him.
passages.sermon:
If you find an animal that belongs to your brother, and your brother does not live near you, or you do not know who he is, you must take the animal into your house.
You must keep the animal with you.
You must keep it until your brother looks for it.
When your brother comes to claim it, you must return the animal to him.
passages.original: וְאִם־ לֹ֨א קָר֥וֹב אָחִ֛יךָ אֵלֶ֖יךָ וְלֹ֣א יְדַעְתּ֑וֹ וַאֲסַפְתּוֹ֙ אֶל־ תּ֣וֹךְ בֵּיתֶ֔ךָ וְהָיָ֣ה עִמְּךָ֗ עַ֣ד דְּרֹ֤שׁ אָחִ֙יךָ֙ אֹת֔וֹ וַהֲשֵׁבֹת֖וֹ לֽוֹ׃

passages.text: And you shall do the same for his donkey, his cloak, or anything your brother has lost and you have found. You must not ignore it.
passages.sermon:
God gave Israel laws about lost property.
\r\nIf you find your brother’s donkey, treat it as you would his ox or sheep.
\r\nIf you find your brother’s cloak, treat it the same way.
\r\nIf you find anything your brother has lost, treat it the same way.
\r\nReturn what you find to your brother.
\r\nDo not ignore what belongs to your brother.
\r\nYou must not hide from your responsibility.
passages.original: וְכֵ֧ן תַּעֲשֶׂ֣ה לַחֲמֹר֗וֹ וְכֵ֣ן תַּעֲשֶׂה֮ לְשִׂמְלָתוֹ֒ וְכֵ֣ן תַּעֲשֶׂ֜ה לְכָל־ אֲבֵדַ֥ת אָחִ֛יךָ אֲשֶׁר־ תֹּאבַ֥ד מִמֶּ֖נּוּ וּמְצָאתָ֑הּ לֹ֥א תוּכַ֖ל לְהִתְעַלֵּֽם׃ס

passages.text: If you see your brother’s donkey or ox fallen on the road, you must not ignore it; you must help him lift it up.
passages.sermon: If you see your brother’s donkey fallen on the road, you must not ignore it.\r\nIf you see your brother’s ox fallen on the road, you must not ignore it.\r\nYou must help your brother lift up his animal.
passages.original: לֹא־ תִרְאֶה֩ אֶת־ חֲמ֨וֹר אָחִ֜יךָ א֤וֹ שׁוֹרוֹ֙ נֹפְלִ֣ים בַּדֶּ֔רֶךְ וְהִתְעַלַּמְתָּ֖ מֵהֶ֑ם הָקֵ֥ם תָּקִ֖ים עִמּֽוֹ׃ס

passages.text: A woman must not wear men’s clothing, and a man must not wear women’s clothing, for whoever does these things is detestable to the LORD your God.
passages.sermon:
God commands His people to obey His laws.
A woman must not wear clothing that belongs to a man.
A man must not wear clothing that belongs to a woman.
Anyone who does these things acts in a way that the LORD your God hates.
passages.original: לֹא־ יִהְיֶ֤ה כְלִי־ גֶ֙בֶר֙ עַל־ אִשָּׁ֔ה וְלֹא־ יִלְבַּ֥שׁ גֶּ֖בֶר שִׂמְלַ֣ת אִשָּׁ֑ה כִּ֧י תוֹעֲבַ֛ת יְהוָ֥ה אֱלֹהֶ֖יךָ כָּל־ עֹ֥שֵׂה אֵֽלֶּה׃פ

passages.text: If you come across a bird’s nest with chicks or eggs, either in a tree or on the ground along the road, and the mother is sitting on the chicks or eggs, you must not take the mother along with the young.
passages.sermon:
You may find a bird’s nest while you walk along the road.
The nest may be in a tree.
The nest may be on the ground.
The nest may have chicks.
The nest may have eggs.
The mother bird may be sitting on the chicks.
The mother bird may be sitting on the eggs.
Do not take the mother bird together with the young.
passages.original: כִּ֣י יִקָּרֵ֣א קַן־ צִפּ֣וֹר׀ לְפָנֶ֡יךָ בַּדֶּ֜רֶךְ בְּכָל־ עֵ֣ץ׀ א֣וֹ עַל־ הָאָ֗רֶץ אֶפְרֹחִים֙ א֣וֹ בֵיצִ֔ים וְהָאֵ֤ם רֹבֶ֙צֶת֙ עַל־ הָֽאֶפְרֹחִ֔ים א֖וֹ עַל־ הַבֵּיצִ֑ים לֹא־ תִקַּ֥ח הָאֵ֖ם עַל־ הַבָּנִֽים׃

passages.text: You may take the young, but be sure to let the mother go, so that it may be well with you and that you may prolong your days.
passages.sermon:
God gives this command to His people.
If you find a bird’s nest with young birds or eggs, you may take the young for yourself.
You must let the mother bird go free.
If you obey this command, it will go well with you.
You will live a long life.
passages.original: שַׁלֵּ֤חַ תְּשַׁלַּח֙ אֶת־ הָאֵ֔ם וְאֶת־ הַבָּנִ֖ים תִּֽקַּֽח־ לָ֑ךְ לְמַ֙עַן֙ יִ֣יטַב לָ֔ךְ וְהַאֲרַכְתָּ֖ יָמִֽים׃ס

passages.text: If you build a new house, you are to construct a railing around your roof, so that you do not bring bloodguilt on your house if someone falls from it.
passages.sermon:
If you build a new house, you must make a railing for your roof.
The railing will protect people from falling.
If someone falls from your roof, you will not be guilty of their blood.
God commands you to prevent harm to others in your home.
passages.original: כִּ֤י תִבְנֶה֙ בַּ֣יִת חָדָ֔שׁ וְעָשִׂ֥יתָ מַעֲקֶ֖ה לְגַגֶּ֑ךָ וְלֹֽא־ תָשִׂ֤ים דָּמִים֙ בְּבֵיתֶ֔ךָ כִּֽי־ יִפֹּ֥ל הַנֹּפֵ֖ל מִמֶּֽנּוּ׃ס

passages.text: Do not plant your vineyard with two types of seed; if you do, the entire harvest will be defiled —both the crop you plant and the fruit of your vineyard.
passages.sermon:
God gave Israel laws for their daily life.
God commanded the people about their vineyards.
Do not plant your vineyard with two types of seed.
If you plant two types of seed, you will defile the whole harvest.
Both the crop you plant and the fruit of your vineyard will become defiled.
passages.original: לֹא־ תִזְרַ֥ע כַּרְמְךָ֖ כִּלְאָ֑יִם פֶּן־ תִּקְדַּ֗שׁ הַֽמְלֵאָ֤ה הַזֶּ֙רַע֙ אֲשֶׁ֣ר תִּזְרָ֔ע וּתְבוּאַ֖ת הַכָּֽרֶם׃ס

passages.text: Do not plow with an ox and a donkey yoked together.
passages.sermon:
God gave Israel laws for daily life.
God commanded the people about farming.
Do not plow your field with an ox and a donkey yoked together.
Use only animals of the same kind together for plowing.
passages.original: לֹֽא־ תַחֲרֹ֥שׁ בְּשׁוֹר־ וּבַחֲמֹ֖ר יַחְדָּֽו׃ס

passages.text: Do not wear clothes of wool and linen woven together.
passages.sermon:
God gave Israel laws for daily life.
\r\nGod commanded the people about their clothing.
\r\nDo not wear clothing made from both wool and linen woven together.
\r\nWear only clothing made from one kind of material.
passages.original: לֹ֤א תִלְבַּשׁ֙ שַֽׁעַטְנֵ֔ז צֶ֥מֶר וּפִשְׁתִּ֖ים יַחְדָּֽו׃ס

passages.text: You are to make tassels on the four corners of the cloak you wear.
passages.sermon:
God commands the Israelites to obey His laws.
God tells you to make tassels.
You must attach the tassels to your cloak.
Your cloak must have four corners.
You must put one tassel on each corner.
You must wear this cloak to cover yourself.
passages.original: גְּדִלִ֖ים תַּעֲשֶׂה־ לָּ֑ךְ עַל־ אַרְבַּ֛ע כַּנְפ֥וֹת כְּסוּתְךָ֖ אֲשֶׁ֥ר תְּכַסֶּה־ בָּֽהּ׃ס

passages.text: Suppose a man marries a woman, has relations with her, and comes to hate her, and he then accuses her of shameful conduct and gives her a bad name, saying, “I married this woman and had relations with her, but I discovered she was not a virgin.”
passages.sermon:
A man marries a woman.
He has relations with her.
He begins to hate her.
He accuses her of shameful conduct.
He gives her a bad name.
He says, “I married this woman.
I had relations with her.
I discovered she was not a virgin.”
passages.original: כִּֽי־ יִקַּ֥ח אִ֖ישׁ אִשָּׁ֑ה וּבָ֥א אֵלֶ֖יהָ וּשְׂנֵאָֽהּ׃ וְשָׂ֥ם לָהּ֙ עֲלִילֹ֣ת דְּבָרִ֔ים וְהוֹצִ֥יא עָלֶ֖יהָ שֵׁ֣ם רָ֑ע וְאָמַ֗ר אֶת־ הָאִשָּׁ֤ה הַזֹּאת֙ לָקַ֔חְתִּי וָאֶקְרַ֣ב אֵלֶ֔יהָ וְלֹא־ מָצָ֥אתִי לָ֖הּ בְּתוּלִֽים׃

passages.text: Then the young woman’s father and mother shall bring the proof of her virginity to the city elders at the gate and say to the elders, “I gave my daughter in marriage to this man, but he has come to hate her.
passages.sermon:
The young woman’s father and mother must act.
They must bring proof of her virginity.
They must go to the city elders at the gate.
The father must speak to the elders.
He must say, “I gave my daughter to this man as a wife.
He now hates her.”
passages.original: וְלָקַ֛ח אֲבִ֥י הַנַּעַר וְאִמָּ֑הּ וְהוֹצִ֜יאוּ אֶת־ בְּתוּלֵ֧י הַנַּעַר אֶל־ זִקְנֵ֥י הָעִ֖יר הַשָּֽׁעְרָה׃ וְאָמַ֛ר אֲבִ֥י הַנַּעַר אֶל־ הַזְּקֵנִ֑ים אֶת־ בִּתִּ֗י נָתַ֜תִּי לָאִ֥ישׁ הַזֶּ֛ה לְאִשָּׁ֖ה וַיִּשְׂנָאֶֽהָ׃

passages.text: And now he has accused her of shameful conduct, saying, ‘I discovered that your daughter was not a virgin.’ But here is the proof of her virginity.” And they shall spread out the cloth before the city elders.
passages.sermon:
The man has accused the young woman of shameful conduct.
He says, “I discovered that your daughter was not a virgin.”
The parents present proof of her virginity.
They spread out the cloth before the elders of the city.
passages.original: וְהִנֵּה־ ה֡וּא שָׂם֩ עֲלִילֹ֨ת דְּבָרִ֜ים לֵאמֹ֗ר לֹֽא־ מָצָ֤אתִי לְבִתְּךָ֙ בְּתוּלִ֔ים וְאֵ֖לֶּה בְּתוּלֵ֣י בִתִּ֑י וּפָֽרְשׂוּ֙ הַשִּׂמְלָ֔ה לִפְנֵ֖י זִקְנֵ֥י הָעִֽיר׃

passages.text: Then the elders of that city shall take the man and punish him.
passages.sermon: The elders of that city are leaders and judges.\r\nThey will take the man who made the false accusation.\r\nThey will punish him.
passages.original: וְלָֽקְח֛וּ זִקְנֵ֥י הָֽעִיר־ הַהִ֖וא אֶת־ הָאִ֑ישׁ וְיִסְּר֖וּ אֹתֽוֹ׃

passages.text: They are also to fine him a hundred shekels of silver and give them to the young woman’s father, because this man has given a virgin of Israel a bad name. And she shall remain his wife; he must not divorce her as long as he lives.
passages.sermon:
The elders of the city must punish the man.
They must fine him one hundred shekels of silver.
They must give this money to the father of the young woman.
The man gave a bad name to a virgin of Israel.
The young woman must remain his wife.
He must not divorce her for the rest of his life.
passages.original: וְעָנְשׁ֨וּ אֹת֜וֹ מֵ֣אָה כֶ֗סֶף וְנָתְנוּ֙ לַאֲבִ֣י הַֽנַּעֲרָ֔ה כִּ֤י הוֹצִיא֙ שֵׁ֣ם רָ֔ע עַ֖ל בְּתוּלַ֣ת יִשְׂרָאֵ֑ל וְלֽוֹ־ תִהְיֶ֣ה לְאִשָּׁ֔ה לֹא־ יוּכַ֥ל לְשַּׁלְּחָ֖הּ כָּל־ יָמָֽיו׃ס

passages.text: If, however, this accusation is true, and no proof of the young woman’s virginity can be found, she shall be brought to the door of her father’s house, and there the men of her city will stone her to death. For she has committed an outrage in Israel by being promiscuous in her father’s house. So you must purge the evil from among you.
passages.sermon:
If the accusation is true, the young woman is not a virgin.
The people must bring the young woman to the door of her father’s house.
The men of her city must stone her with stones until she dies.
She has done a disgraceful thing in Israel.
She was promiscuous in her father’s house.
You must remove the evil from among you.
passages.original: וְאִם־ אֱמֶ֣ת הָיָ֔ה הַדָּבָ֖ר הַזֶּ֑ה לֹא־ נִמְצְא֥וּ בְתוּלִ֖ים לַנַּעַר׃ וְהוֹצִ֨יאוּ אֶת־ הַנַּעַר אֶל־ פֶּ֣תַח בֵּית־ אָבִ֗יהָ וּסְקָלוּהָ֩ אַנְשֵׁ֨י עִירָ֤הּ בָּאֲבָנִים֙ וָמֵ֔תָה כִּֽי־ עָשְׂתָ֤ה נְבָלָה֙ בְּיִשְׂרָאֵ֔ל לִזְנ֖וֹת בֵּ֣ית אָבִ֑יהָ וּבִֽעַרְתָּ֥ הָרָ֖ע מִקִּרְבֶּֽךָ׃ס

passages.text: If a man is found lying with another man’s wife, both the man who slept with her and the woman must die. You must purge the evil from Israel.
passages.sermon:
God gave Israel laws about marriage and faithfulness.
If someone finds a man lying with a married woman, this is adultery.
The man has slept with another man’s wife.
The woman is married to someone else.
Both the man and the woman must die.
This punishment removes evil from Israel.
passages.original: כִּֽי־ יִמָּצֵ֨א אִ֜ישׁ שֹׁכֵ֣ב׀ עִם־ אִשָּׁ֣ה בְעֻֽלַת־ בַּ֗עַל וּמֵ֙תוּ֙ גַּם־ שְׁנֵיהֶ֔ם הָאִ֛ישׁ הַשֹּׁכֵ֥ב עִם־ הָאִשָּׁ֖ה וְהָאִשָּׁ֑ה וּבִֽעַרְתָּ֥ הָרָ֖ע מִיִּשְׂרָאֵֽל׃ס

passages.text: If there is a virgin pledged in marriage to a man, and another man encounters her in the city and sleeps with her, you must take both of them out to the gate of that city and stone them to death—the young woman because she did not cry out in the city, and the man because he has violated his neighbor’s wife. So you must purge the evil from among you.
passages.sermon:
A virgin woman is pledged in marriage to a man.
Another man finds her in the city.
He sleeps with her.
You must take both the woman and the man to the gate of that city.
You must stone both of them with stones.
They will die.
The woman did not cry out in the city.
The man violated his neighbor’s wife.
You must remove the evil from among you.
passages.original: כִּ֤י יִהְיֶה֙ נַעַר בְתוּלָ֔ה מְאֹרָשָׂ֖ה לְאִ֑ישׁ וּמְצָאָ֥הּ אִ֛ישׁ בָּעִ֖יר וְשָׁכַ֥ב עִמָּֽהּ׃ וְהוֹצֵאתֶ֨ם אֶת־ שְׁנֵיהֶ֜ם אֶל־ שַׁ֣עַר׀ הָעִ֣יר הַהִ֗וא וּסְקַלְתֶּ֨ם אֹתָ֥ם בָּאֲבָנִים֮ וָמֵתוּ֒ אֶת־ הַנַּעַר עַל־ דְּבַר֙ אֲשֶׁ֣ר לֹא־ צָעֲקָ֣ה בָעִ֔יר וְאֶ֨ת־ הָאִ֔ישׁ עַל־ דְּבַ֥ר אֲשֶׁר־ עִנָּ֖ה אֶת־ אֵ֣שֶׁת רֵעֵ֑הוּ וּבִֽעַרְתָּ֥ הָרָ֖ע מִקִּרְבֶּֽךָ׃ס

passages.text: But if the man encounters a betrothed woman in the open country, and he overpowers her and lies with her, only the man who has done this must die.
passages.sermon:
A man may find a woman who is promised in marriage.
They are in the open country.
The man seizes the woman.
He lies with her.
The man has done wrong.
Only the man who lay with her must die.
The woman does not die.
passages.original: וְֽאִם־ בַּשָּׂדֶ֞ה יִמְצָ֣א הָאִ֗ישׁ אֶת־ הַנַּעַר הַמְאֹ֣רָשָׂ֔ה וְהֶחֱזִֽיק־ בָּ֥הּ הָאִ֖ישׁ וְשָׁכַ֣ב עִמָּ֑הּ וּמֵ֗ת הָאִ֛ישׁ אֲשֶׁר־ שָׁכַ֥ב עִמָּ֖הּ לְבַדּֽוֹ׃

passages.text: Do nothing to the young woman, because she has committed no sin worthy of death. This case is just like one in which a man attacks his neighbor and murders him.
passages.sermon:
The young woman is innocent.
She has done nothing wrong.
She has not committed a sin that deserves death.
Do not punish her.
This case is like when a man attacks his neighbor and kills him.
The guilt belongs to the attacker, not to the victim.
passages.original: וְלַנַּעַר לֹא־ תַעֲשֶׂ֣ה דָבָ֔ר אֵ֥ין לַנַּעַר חֵ֣טְא מָ֑וֶת כִּ֡י כַּאֲשֶׁר֩ יָק֨וּם אִ֤ישׁ עַל־ רֵעֵ֙הוּ֙ וּרְצָח֣וֹ נֶ֔פֶשׁ כֵּ֖ן הַדָּבָ֥ר הַזֶּֽה׃

passages.text: When he found her in the field, the betrothed woman cried out, but there was no one to save her.
passages.sermon:
A man found a betrothed woman in the field.
The woman was engaged to be married.
She cried out for help.
No one was there to save her.
passages.original: כִּ֥י בַשָּׂדֶ֖ה מְצָאָ֑הּ צָעֲקָ֗ה הַנַּעַר הַמְאֹ֣רָשָׂ֔ה וְאֵ֥ין מוֹשִׁ֖יעַ לָֽהּ׃ס

passages.text: If a man encounters a virgin who is not pledged in marriage, and he seizes her and lies with her, and they are discovered, then the man who lay with her must pay the young woman’s father fifty shekels of silver, and she must become his wife because he has violated her. He must not divorce her as long as he lives.
passages.sermon:
A man finds a young woman.
She is a virgin.
She is not pledged in marriage.
The man seizes her.
He lies with her.
People discover them.
The man who lay with her must pay the young woman’s father fifty shekels of silver.
The young woman must become his wife.
The man has violated her.
He must not divorce her as long as he lives.
passages.original: כִּֽי־ יִמְצָ֣א אִ֗ישׁ נַעַר בְתוּלָה֙ אֲשֶׁ֣ר לֹא־ אֹרָ֔שָׂה וּתְפָשָׂ֖הּ וְשָׁכַ֣ב עִמָּ֑הּ וְנִמְצָֽאוּ׃ וְ֠נָתַן הָאִ֨ישׁ הַשֹּׁכֵ֥ב עִמָּ֛הּ לַאֲבִ֥י הַנַּעַר חֲמִשִּׁ֣ים כָּ֑סֶף וְלֽוֹ־ תִהְיֶ֣ה לְאִשָּׁ֗ה תַּ֚חַת אֲשֶׁ֣ר עִנָּ֔הּ לֹא־ יוּכַ֥ל שַׁלְּחָ֖ה כָּל־ יָמָֽיו׃ס

passages.text: A man is not to marry his father’s wife, so that he will not dishonor his father’s marriage bed.
passages.sermon: A man must not marry his father’s wife.\r\nA man must not dishonor his father’s marriage bed.
passages.original: לֹא־ יִקַּ֥ח אִ֖ישׁ אֶת־ אֵ֣שֶׁת אָבִ֑יו וְלֹ֥א יְגַלֶּ֖ה כְּנַ֥ף אָבִֽיו׃ס
